subject: Recap + Action plan for Zephyr Health inference evaluation
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@zephyrhealth.com>, Priya Shah <priya@zephyrhealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + Action plan for Zephyr Health inference evaluation

Alex / Priya — thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap of what we heard and the proposed action plan so we have a single source of truth going into next week. Please flag anything I missed.

Top pain points & goals (call highlights)
- Latency spikes with current LLM routing during peak ETL windows (avg 600–1,200ms per request; spikes up to 2s)
- Cost variability month-over-month — need a path to predictable unit economics for production inference
- Data governance: audit logs and retention policies required for clinical research workflows
- Goal: pilot Redwood for a 3-month evaluation to validate latency SLOs and running cost per 1M tokens; expand to production for one internal app by Q4 if results align

Proposed action plan (milestones, owners, dates)
1) Technical discovery & infra review — collect workload traces + sample prompts (owner: Alex / Zephyr) — target: 2026-06-17
2) Pilot environment standing up (Redwood Dedicated test pool) — owner: Marcus (Redwood) — target: 2026-06-24
3) Pilot run & acceptance criteria validation (latency, token cost, quality checks) — owner: Camila / Alex — target window: 2026-06-25 to 2026-07-23
4) Procurement & SOW draft (if pilot OK) — owner: Priya (Zephyr) + Redwood sales ops — target: 2026-07-09
5) Executive decision (buy/expand) — decision committee: Alex (CTO), Priya (Head of Procurement), Dr. Ramos (Research Dir.) — target: 2026-07-30

Immediate asks / next steps
- Alex: share traces (s3 link) + list of top 5 endpoints and current QPS profile by 2026-06-17.
- Priya: confirm procurement cadence and any mandatory PO/SLA language we should include by 2026-06-18.
- Marcus: confirm Dedicated test pool capacity and provide a rough cost snapshot by 2026-06-18.
- Camila: I’ll set up a 30-minute alignment call for 2026-06-18 to review traces and finalize pilot config.

Attachments: Zephyr-Eval-Action-Plan-v1.xlsx (action plan table), Redwood-TCO-snapshot.pdf (high-level cost assumptions)

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving. 

—
Camila Reyes

Subject: Re: Recap + Action plan for Zephyr Health inference evaluation

Thanks Camila — nice write-up. Quick confirmations and a couple tweaks from our side.

Confirmed pain & priorities:
- Latency spikes are the blocker for the research app; anything under ~250ms P95 gives the team confidence.
- Cost predictability is critical; we need a clear per-token baseline and a mechanism to cap spend on the pilot.

Milestone updates:
- We can share traces; I’ll drop a shared s3 bucket link by EOD Friday (2026-06-12) — note: data will be redacted to remove PHI, but traces will include timestamps and request sizes.
- Procurement: Priya heads this — procurement window is typically 4–6 weeks for a pilot SOW, but we can fast-track internal approvals if we get a clear cost estimate and pilot term.

Decision committee: adding one more stakeholder — Dr. Clare Ramos (Research Director) needs to sign off on quality criteria.

Two asks from our side: 
1) Can Redwood provide a one-sheet that maps the pilot acceptance criteria to measurable metrics (latency p95 target, cost per 100k tokens, sample eval prompts)?
2) Marcus: any constraints on the Dedicated pool (min capacity, region)? We prefer east-us for colocation.

Thanks — Alex

Quick internal note — cc’ing Tessa for ops:

- Dedicated test pool: we can provision a 2x-A100 equivalent pool in east-us with reserved capacity for the window starting 2026-06-24. Lead time to stand up is ~4 business days once Zephyr signs off on the test config.
- Cost snapshot: attached quick estimate (see Redwood-TCO-snapshot.pdf in Camila’s mail). For the pilot window we can guarantee a spend cap if we include a burst buffer clause — I’ll draft numbers.
- Constraints: KV cache persistence across restarts is supported but we need to confirm sequence-length profiles; if they go above 2k tokens we’ll need a different kernel selection which can affect latency.

I’ll join the 6/18 call to walk through the infra plan.
